en: All the things under discussion.

en: Something tiny, as a pinprick; a very small mark.
A full stop or other terminal punctuation mark.
Point taken; understood; got it.
To extend the index finger in the direction of something in order to show where it is or to draw attention to it.

point.ety:
From Middle English poynt, from Old French point m (“dot; minute amount”), from Latin pūnctum (“a hole punched in; a point, puncture”), substantive use of pūnctus m, perfect passive participle of pungō (“to prick, punch”); alternatively, from Old French pointe f (“sharp tip”), from Latin pūncta f (past participle), all from Proto-Italic *pungō (“to sting, prick”).
Mostly displaced native Middle English ord (“point”), from Old English ord (“point”). Doublet of pointe, ponto, puncto, punctum, punt, and punto.

ex.ja: 話の要点を書き留めなさい。

To be understood or physically read in a specific way.

tell.ety:
From Middle English tellen (“to count, tell”), from Old English tellan (“to count, tell”), from Proto-West Germanic *talljan, from Proto-Germanic *taljaną, *talzijaną (“to count, enumerate”), from Proto-Germanic *talą, *talō (“number, counting”), from Proto-Indo-European *dol- (“calculation, fraud”).

ex.ja: その計画は今のところ未決定である。

once.ety: From Middle English ones, from Old English ānes, a remodelling (after ān (“one”)) of ǣnes, itself an extension of ǣne (“once”) with the genitive suffix -es. Equivalent to one + -s. ex.ja: 設定料金に労務費用は含みません。

To memorize; to put something into memory.

The substance of the atmosphere seen as an agency of freshness.

A piece of metal placed in a horse's mouth and connected to the reins to direct the animal.
To put a bridle upon; to put the bit in the mouth of (a horse).
Having been bitten.

bit.ety:
From Middle English bitte, bite, from Old English bita (“bit; fragment; morsel”) and bite (“a bite; cut”), from Proto-Germanic *bitô and *bitiz; both from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyd- (“to split”). More at bite.

ex.ja: 少しも心配していない。

To come into contact with forcefully and suddenly.

Very successful.

Nicely.

en: In all likelihood.

probably.ety: From Middle English probably, probabily, equivalent to probable + -ly.

en: Yes.

Expressing joy, celebration, glee, etc.

yeah.ety: Colloquial form of yea or yes. Compare nah. Analyzable as yes + -h.

ex.ja: それなら、昨日聞いたわ。

To assign to a class; to classify.
To be grouped or classed.

class.ety:
From Middle French classe, from Latin classis (“a class or division of the people, assembly of people, the whole body of citizens called to arms, the army, the fleet, later a class or division in general”), from Proto-Indo-European *kelh₁- (“to call, shout”). Doublet of clas and classis.

note.ja: ラテン語 clausus（閉じられた）から。clud/clus（閉じる）。閉じる →「閉める」、間が詰まっている →「近い・親しい」。closet（小さな閉じた部屋→物置）も仲間。

An image of an object that is formed in the mind or recalled by the memory.

ex.ja: それは私には馬鹿げたアイディアに思えた。

ex.ja: その新しいプランは我々の考えに基づいている。

ex.ja: いい案があるかも。

en: Between or among nations.
Participated in by two or more nations.
Someone who has represented their country in a particular sport.

past.ety: From Middle English passed, past participle of Middle English passen (“to pass, to go by”), whence Modern English pass.

Sufficient reason.

ex.ja: あらゆる離婚の主たる原因は結婚である。

Appropriate.

Deserved acknowledgment.
A membership fee.

Having the nature or attributes of a human being.

en: One who belongs to a group.
A part of a whole.

Cognate with Scots wast (“west”), North Frisian waast, weest, wäst (“west”), Saterland Frisian Wääste (“west”), West Frisian and Dutch west (“west”), German West (“west”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk vest (“west”), Faroese and Icelandic vestur (“west”), Swedish väst, väster (“west”); also with Irish feascar, feasgar (“even

ex.en: The town is to the west of London.
ex.ja: ロンドンの西に位置する町です。

ex.en: A Mr. West called while you were out.
ex.ja: 留守中にウェストという人から電話があったよ。

ex.en: The company is located on the West Coast.
ex.ja: その会社は西海岸にあります。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「夕方・日の沈む方角」。ラテン語 vesper（夕方）と同じ祖先。

en: Agreement of opinion, will, or action.
Agreement in pitch and tone; harmony, musical concord.
To make to agree or correspond; to suit one thing to another; to adjust.
To bring (people) to an agreement; to reconcile, settle, adjust or harmonize.

accord.ety: From Middle English accord, from Old French acort, from acorder (see verb below).

ex.en: According to Mike, Mac bought a new car.
ex.ja: マイクによれば、マックは新しい車を買ったそうだ。

ex.en: According to the paper, it will snow tomorrow.
ex.ja: 新聞によれば明日は雪だそうです。

ex.en: According to the newspaper, it will rain today.
ex.ja: 新聞によると今日は雨が降ります。

note.ja: ac（〜へ）+ cord（心）。心を〜に合わせる →「一致（する）」。according to（〜に一致して→〜によれば）。record（心に呼び戻す→記録する）、cordial（心からの）も同じ cor。

en: Such as one may avail oneself of; capable of being used for the accomplishment of a purpose.
Readily obtainable.

available.ety: From Middle English available, avayllable, avayleable, equivalent of avail + -able.

ex.en: This video is not available in your country.
ex.ja: この動画は、お住まいの国では公開されていません。

ex.en: This book is available at one shop only.
ex.ja: この本はただ一軒の店でだけ入手できる。

ex.en: We have little money available for the research.
ex.ja: その研究に使える金はほとんどないんだ。

note.ja: a（〜へ）+ vail（強い・価値がある）+ able。役に立つ価値がある →「利用できる・手が空いている」。value と同じ val。
